**To**
The Station House Officer
[TO CONFIRM: Name of Police Station], [TO CONFIRM: District], Madhya Pradesh

---

**Subject:** Complaint for registration of FIR regarding theft of motorcycle worth ₹60,000/- from hostel parking — offence under Section 303 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

---

## I. COMPLAINANT DETAILS

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Name | [TO CONFIRM: Full name of complainant] |
| Father's / Husband's Name | [TO CONFIRM] |
| Address | [TO CONFIRM: Full residential address] |
| Mobile Number | [TO CONFIRM] |

---

## II. DATE, TIME AND PLACE OF INCIDENT

- **Date of theft:** On or around **13 September 2026** (approximately one week before the complaint)
- **Time of theft:** [TO CONFIRM: approximate time, if known]
- **Place of theft:** Hostel parking area, [TO CONFIRM: full address / name of hostel]

---

## III. FACTS

1. The complainant is the registered owner of a motorcycle bearing registration number **[TO CONFIRM]**, make and model **[TO CONFIRM]**, Engine No. **[TO CONFIRM]**, Chassis No. **[TO CONFIRM]**, valued at approximately **₹60,000/- (Rupees Sixty Thousand only)**.

2. On or around **13 September 2026**, the complainant had lawfully parked the said motorcycle in the parking area of **[TO CONFIRM: name/address of hostel]**.

3. When the complainant returned to the parking area at approximately **[TO CONFIRM: time]**, the motorcycle was found missing. It is believed that an unknown person or persons dishonestly took the said motorcycle out of the complainant's possession without the complainant's consent.

4. The complainant made enquiries in the vicinity but could not locate the motorcycle or identify the perpetrator(s). **[TO CONFIRM: whether any witnesses were present or CCTV cameras exist at the location]**

5. The complainant thereafter approached **[TO CONFIRM: name of police station]** on **[TO CONFIRM: date of approach to police station]** to lodge a complaint. The officer-in-charge of the said police station **refused to register the FIR** without assigning any lawful reason, in violation of Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS).

6. Theft of a motor vehicle is a cognizable offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS). The police are statutorily bound to register an FIR upon receipt of information of a cognizable offence, except in cases falling within the limited preliminary-enquiry exception applicable to offences punishable with imprisonment between three and seven years — **[TO CONFIRM: supervising advocate to confirm that the punishment range for theft under BNS Section 303 in the facts of this case does not attract the preliminary-enquiry exception under BNSS Section 173]**.

---

| Section | Act | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **303** | BNS 2023 | The unknown accused dishonestly took the complainant's motorcycle, a movable property, out of the complainant's possession without consent, constituting theft. |

---

In view of the above facts, the complainant most respectfully prays that Your Honour:

1. Register a First Information Report (FIR) against the unknown accused under Section 303 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, forthwith;
2. Order an immediate investigation to trace and recover the stolen motorcycle;
3. Provide the complainant with a free copy of the FIR as is the complainant's right under BNSS 2023; and
4. Grant such other relief as this Hon'ble authority deems fit in the facts and circumstances of the case.

---

1. Copy of ID proof of complainant — **[TO CONFIRM: type]**
2. Copy of Registration Certificate (RC) of the stolen motorcycle
3. Copy of Insurance documents of the motorcycle (if available)
4. Copy of Purchase invoice / valuation document for the motorcycle (if available)
5. Photographs of the parking area / CCTV footage (if available)
6. Names and contact details of witnesses, if any — **[TO CONFIRM]**
7. Any other document evidencing ownership or the fact of theft — **[TO CONFIRM]**

---

**Place:** [TO CONFIRM]
**Date:** 20 September 2026

**Signature of Complainant:** ___________________________
**Name:** [TO CONFIRM]

sections.why: The unknown accused dishonestly took the complainant's motorcycle (movable property) out of the complainant's possession without consent, constituting theft.

The police officer-in-charge refused to register an FIR for this cognizable offence; registration is mandatory where the offence falls outside the preliminary-enquiry exception (offences punishable with 3–7 years imprisonment) — supervising advocate to confirm this exception does not apply on these facts.
The complainant may register a Zero FIR at any police station in Madhya Pradesh regardless of territorial jurisdiction, which will then be transferred to the jurisdictional station.

The local police station has refused to register the FIR, entitling the complainant to send the substance of the complaint in writing to the Superintendent of Police, who may direct a competent officer to investigate.
If the SP also fails to act, the complainant may apply to the Magistrate to order a police investigation into this cognizable offence.

Supervising advocate to confirm the punishment range for theft under BNS Section 303 to ensure the preliminary-enquiry exception under BNSS Section 173 does not apply on these facts.
Attempt to register the FIR at the local police station first, carrying the finalised draft complaint.

Under BNSS Section 173(1) (Zero FIR), the complainant may register an FIR at ANY police station in Madhya Pradesh regardless of territorial jurisdiction — the FIR will be transferred to the jurisdictional station; a free copy of the FIR is the complainant's right.

Since the station has refused, send the SP letter (drafted above) under BNSS Section 173(4) by registered post with acknowledgement due to the Superintendent of Police of the concerned district; retain the postal receipt and a copy of the letter.
Alternatively, visit the SP office in person and obtain a date-stamped acknowledgement of receipt of the written complaint.
The complainant may also file an e-FIR for vehicle theft on the MP Police citizen portal: https://mppolice.gov.in
If the SP does not act within a reasonable time, the complainant may apply to the Magistrate under BNSS Section 175(3) for an order directing police investigation.
No fee is payable at any stage for lodging an FIR.
There is no statutory limitation period for cognizable offences; however, file as soon as possible to aid investigation and vehicle tracing.
